name: Breeze Companion 0.3.2 — LAN hosting and custom voices
notes:
Companion 0.3.2 adds LAN access to the browser UI and lets you add named custom voices from your own reference recordings.

### LAN browser hosting

On Windows, open PowerShell in the extracted package folder and run:

```powershell
.\breeze-companion.cmd --web-host 0.0.0.0 --no-browser
```

On Linux, use `breeze-pny serve --web --web-host 0.0.0.0 --no-browser` with the installed launcher. Open the complete session link using the server's LAN IPv4 address, keeping the port and `#token`. Allow TCP port **18793** on the server's private-network firewall. You can bind one specific IPv4 address instead of all interfaces.

Localhost remains the default. The UI retains its session token and Host/Origin checks. Use a trusted LAN: this is HTTP, and the session link allows model and voice management. Add `--host 0.0.0.0` only if the game API should also be available over the LAN on port **18792**. Browser generation needs only the web port; native synthesis stays on loopback.

### Named custom voices

In **Voices → Add voice**, enter a name and voice ID, import a clean recording, select 0.25–30 seconds and enter its exact transcript. Generate a preview, listen, then save. The new name appears in **Generate**, and API clients use its ID as `character_id`.

Added voices use the base model without a pony LoRA adapter. They survive restarts and compatible updates; **Undo last save** restores the previous pack. Existing reference replacement still preserves the selected character's adapter/settings. Adding a voice does not create a new game character. The UI also shows the appropriate API address when opened over the LAN.

### Downloads and upgrade

| Platform | Companion archive |
| --- | --- |
| Windows x86_64 | `breeze-tts-pny-0.3.2-windows-x86_64.zip` |
| Linux x86_64 | `breeze-tts-pny-server-0.3.2-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |

New installations also need **`breeze-pny-curated-voices-20261115.tar.gz`**, attached below. Windows includes Python and the native runtime; Linux needs Python 3.11+ and the documented system dependencies.

Upgrading from **0.3.0 or 0.3.1** reuses the same voice archive, model files, patched 0.1.6 runtime and game mod **0.1.3**. Stop Companion before updating:

- **Windows:** copy the new package contents into your existing package folder, preserving `companion/`, then run `setup.cmd --update`.
- **Linux:** from the new extracted folder, run `python3 installer/install.py --prefix /path/to/existing/installation --update`.

Setup preserves the selected model, ports and compatible personal references. Restart with your desired flags and open the newly printed session link; the page header should read **0.3.2**. [Full guide](https://github.com/ponywizard/breeze-tts-pny/blob/v0.3.2/docs/COMPANION.md). For 0.2.1 installations, follow the [earlier migration instructions](https://github.com/ponywizard/breeze-tts-pny/blob/v0.3.2/docs/COMPANION.md#upgrade-from-021).

### Validation

- 81 Python tests pass on Linux and under bundled Windows Python/Wine (five expected Windows skips), including authentication, named voices, restart, undo and update preservation.
- Chromium workflows pass through localhost and the host's LAN IPv4 address, covering custom voice creation/generation/reload/undo alongside the existing generation, reference, model, seed/direction and mobile checks.
- Packaged Linux and Windows/Wine installations upgrade from 0.3.1, reuse the existing model and serve the authenticated LAN UI. The packaged Linux Q8 renderer registers, auditions and generates a new custom voice, then retains it through another packaged update and restart.
- Native Windows browser/firewall/GPU and second-computer LAN checks remain with community testers. No new game/VR playtest or voice-quality claim is made.

[Validation details](https://github.com/ponywizard/breeze-tts-pny/blob/v0.3.2/docs/SERVER_VALIDATION.md). `SHA256SUMS`, build receipts and `RELEASE-MANIFEST.json` identify the published artifacts and source commit.
